title: Variant heatmap and ops crumbs deploy playbook (Oct 2026) - WIP
content:
Purpose:
Quick working playbook for running a variant-driven rollout with a visual heatmap, short operator cues ("ops crumbs"), and a compact calendar. This doc is intentionally pragmatic — crib notes for a 48–72 hour launch window where we want fast decisions and minimal friction.

Scope:
- Applies to minor and medium releases that change routing, model variant pins, or autoscaling thresholds.
- Not for major schema changes, database migrations, or multi-day infra refactors.
- Intended audience: release conductor, on-call SRE, serving-runtime lead, product PM on-call.

One-line objective:
Move 20% -> 100% traffic across three regional cohorts with staged variant pinning and automated rollback gates in under 36 hours while preserving 99th p50 latency SLOs and no customer-impact incidents > Sev2.

Variant heatmap (operational view):
- Columns: Cohort (NA, EU, APAC), Variant (v1-small, v1-quant, v2-fp16), Load slice (0-5%, 5-20%, 20-100%), Observed p50/p95 latency, Error rate, Token cost delta.
- Use the heatmap to decide fast: red = immediate halt, amber = hold and observe, green = proceed.
- Initial seeding: NA->v2-fp16 at 5%, EU->v1-quant at 5%, APAC remain on v1-small at 0%.
- Key thresholds: p95 latency +20% over baseline OR error rate > 0.5% -> revert slice. Token cost increase tolerated up to 12% for quality gain; product PM signoff required beyond that.

Ops crumbs (short actionable notes for operators):
- Crumb: "Keep it small" = cap individual slice to <= 20% until warmed for 45 min.
- Crumb: "Watch the tail" = focus p95 and 99, not just p50.
- Crumb: "Safe lane" = predefine fallback variant (v1-quant) per region and ensure cache warming for 10 minutes before progressing.
- Crumb: "Kill switch" = traffic-router rollback (route->fallback) is primed at all times; remember the retainment window is 5 minutes.
- Crumb: "Comms short" = PM + SE + SRE on a 1min Slack channel ring when going beyond 25% each region.

Preflight checklist (must be green before any traffic change):
- [ ] Telemetry hooks live and validated (latency, errors, token_count, model-id label).
- [ ] Canary cluster smoke passed (sample 500 traces, no more than 2 failures).
- [ ] Fallback pinned and verified for quick routing swap.
- [ ] Runbook visible to on-call in the ops channel and in pager schedule.
- [ ] Release notes draft posted to customer-notes-slate and internal comms.
- [ ] Feature flags verified in config service and rollback policy set to immediate if gate trips.

Compact rollout calendar (48-hour plan):
Day 0 (T = 0) - Preparation window (2–4 hours before first slice)
- Confirm preflight checklist. Final signoffs: Release Conductor (Aisha), SRE lead (Miguel), PM on-call (Renee).
- Warm KV caches on fallback variant for 10 minutes.
- Post initial release note snippet: "beta routing enabled for select cohorts".

T+0h - Seed phase (first 2 hours)
- NA: +5% to v2-fp16. EU: +5% to v1-quant. APAC: unchanged.
- Observe 30m windows; auto-escalate if p99 > baseline*1.25 or errors spike > 0.3%.

T+2h -> T+6h - Gentle ramp
- NA: 5% -> 20% over two steps (5% -> 10% -> 20%) spaced 60m apart.
- EU: 5% -> 10% -> hold. APAC: hold at 0% while monitoring global impact.
- If any amber signals persist for >45m, pause and perform focused replay tests.

T+6h -> T+18h - Regional expansion
- NA: 20% -> 50% if green lanes. EU: 10% -> 30% if green. APAC: start 5% -> 10% if no bleed from NA/EU.
- Telemetry gating enforced: automated gate checks every 15 minutes.

T+18h -> T+36h - Full conversion (if all green)
- Ramp to 100% per region in controlled steps. Post conversion: 2h warm observation, then finalize release notes.

Telemetry and sampling strategy:
- Baseline signals: p50, p95, p99 latency for inference, error count (4xx/5xx), user-facing error rate, token-per-call distribution, cost-per-token delta.
- Sampling: 100% metrics, 1% traces for early seeding rising to 5% during heavy ramp. Keep request-level logs for rollbacks (truncate PII).
- Alerting: realtime Slack notify if p99 > baseline*1.25 OR error rate > 0.5% OR token-cost delta > 20% sustained for 30m.

Rollback decision tree (fast path):
- Immediate revert: any Sev1 incident or sustained p99 > baseline*1.5 for 10m.
- Soft revert: sustain error rate > 0.8% for 15m OR unexplainable quality regression flagged by product evals.
- Cost-driven revert: token-cost delta > 35% with no measured quality improvement (PM decision).

Release notes (internal draft template):
- Title: "Oct 2026: Variant routing experiment — staged rollout"
- Summary: short blurb, what changed, target cohorts, expected visible impacts.
- Customer impact: none expected; fallback available. If any, list customer-facing mitigations.
- Rollout timeline: bullets for seed -> ramp -> full.
- Known issues: e.g., "cold-cache latency observed for variant v2-fp16 under small burst patterns".

Post-release quick debrief (to be filled after closure):
- Who: list names on shift for the window.
- What went well (3 bullets).
- What surprised us (3 bullets).
- Telemetry anomalies (links to dashboards).
- Action items (owner + ETA).

Postmortem triggers:
- Any incident > Sev2.
- Customer-facing outage or degraded experience for > 30 minutes.
- Revert required after > 25% traffic change with root cause unknown.

Known risks and mitigations (working list):
- Risk: regional asymmetric load causes warm-up skew. Mitigation: staggered ramp and per-region cache warming.
- Risk: model quantization introduces rare tokenization edge-cases. Mitigation: regression eval set run preflight; spot-check 50 queries across cohorts.
- Risk: CI artifact mismatch in docker tags. Mitigation: immutable image tags and digest verification step in preflight.

Open action items before T+0:
- [Aisha] finalize short customer-facing note and link to KB article. Due: 2026-10-01.
- [Miguel] verify routing fallback automation test (runbook test id RF-22). Due: 2026-09-30.
- [Samir] add token-cost alert to release gates (threshold draft: 20%). Due: 2026-10-02.

Notes to self / rough thoughts (scratchpad):
- Consider adding a tiny canary that uses mirrored traffic with deterministic subset of queries for behavioral checks. Might reduce space for surprises.
- If v2-fp16 shows 10–15% quality improvement at 12% cost delta, push to product for scale decision; document ROI.

Quick links (ops shortcuts):
- Traffic router UI: https://internal.router.redwood/variants
- Heatmap dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood/variant-heatmap/oct-2026
- Rollout gating job: https://ci.redwood/jobs/rollout-gates/1427

Last edits: 2026-10-05 by Aisha Patel.
Status: WIP — keep it short and actionable.

-- end of playbook --
